description:
## Functional specifications and files
Extend lib/zaq/agent/tools/web/browsing.ex and test/zaq/agent/tools/web/browsing_test.exs. Remove allowed_domains from the LLM-facing schema; reject or ignore legacy/model-injected values without allowing policy override. Obtain configured policy through supported Engine configuration events, pass arguments separately to the existing Command runner, and make empty policy explicitly override inherited AGENT_BROWSER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS/config defaults. Verify pinned CLI behavior for an explicit empty list before selecting invocation details; extend existing command environment options only if required, without shell interpolation. Config unavailable/malformed returns an error, not unrestricted browsing.

## Scope and description contract
Preserve session(params, context) precedence and shared fallback for this release; no identity binding, daemon tracking, hot updates or new reset operation. GitHub #825 owns session work. Describe open -> snapshot/text -> current-ref interaction; keep the same explicit session throughout; if defaulting, keep omitting session rather than inventing one mid-task. Explain CLI success is not page success, read text body for empty/Blocked pages and verify URL after navigation/submission. Domains are administrator controlled; do not advise the model to broaden policy or bypass restrictions. Document screenshot capture+storage behavior when the screenshot step lands. Preserve existing command behavior and argument-injection defenses.

## Tests to add before implementation / branches
Schema contains no allowed_domains; malicious/legacy parameters cannot widen configured policy; blank policy is truly unrestricted at fresh startup even with inherited env restrictions; nonblank list and missing-config/error paths; existing explicit/default session regression; unsupported command, timeout/nonzero and argument separation regressions. Real pinned-browser tests cover allow/deny and redirects using deterministic fixture hosts. Existing running daemons may retain policy until a full Agent-container restart; test/document rather than silently claiming hot application.

## Action reuse assessment
Extend existing Browsing Action and System.Command execution; no replacement browser SDK, generic browser proxy, custom daemon manager or copied command runner. Consumers remain tool and workflow Action invocation under existing boundaries. No automatic elevation.

## Mocking and documentation
Reuse command-boundary fixture binary for unit tests and existing opt-in real-browser harness for integration. Inject runtime dependencies via established public-boundary carriers, no global config mutation. Update Action schema/moduledoc, docs/services/agent.md and system-config operational notes. Agent harness checks are required.

## Execution constraints and policies
Planning only; do not mark complete without implementation evidence. Future implementation uses a new branch in the current worktree, not another worktree; do not commit/push without authorization. Read AGENTS.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/agent-tools.md, docs/action-reuse.md and docs/testing-approach.md. Read each affected module @moduledoc and relevant service owner before editing. Follow the authoritative validation lifecycle rather than inventing alternate gates. Preserve existing assertions. New feature E2E authoring is deferred until the separate human approval issue closes.
title: [zaq-xfj.3] Make browser policy admin-owned and clarify tool descriptions
